title: spec review: S3c memory feeds skills and strategy: recurring procedural memory becomes learned-skill candidates, promoted skills are referenced from memory, workflow strategy outcomes live as structured WARM records with a Planner query (P30, P31)
spec:
orchestrator/skill_learning.py: add candidates_from_memory(root) using memory_store.search over kinds gotcha and decision: group records by shared components (at least 3 records over at least 2 distinct dates) whose bodies contain procedural language (imperative verbs such as run, check, set, use, never, always, before, after) and produce learned-skill proposals through the existing proposal path (same shape and quarantine/testing lifecycle as today's learned skills; provenance memory with the record ids). When a proposal's skill is promoted to active, memory_store.add records a tag skill:<skill_id> on each source record and memory_hot renders such records as one line pointing at the skill instead of the full body. orchestrator/strategy.py: at merge time (the daemon's merge_reviewed path already derives strategy rows) write one memory_store record kind strategy per merged execute task: title '<task_class> <band> <strategy name>', tags task_class:<x>, band:<b>, strategy:<name>, outcome first_pass|fix_rounds:<n>, body with tokens, duration, executor, fix rounds; source_task and source_goal set. CLI `orchestrator memory strategies [--task-class x] [--band b] [--json]` aggregates strategy records: per strategy name the count, first-pass rate, median tokens and duration, so the Planner asks what worked for this kind of task without reading retrospectives. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/17-memory-skills-strategy.md.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Task worktrees carry no .orchestrator runs, tasks or decision_log state: tests use synthetic fixtures; for any measured numbers in docs run read-only against /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/.orchestrator via an explicit root argument. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Contracts of the earlier modules: .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and docs/hermes-hardening/*.md on this branch; read the merged modules before building on them.

risks.issue: Spec claims 'the daemon's merge_reviewed path already derives strategy rows' but daemon.py never imports or calls orchestrator/strategy.py today; the only callers of strategy.py are cli.py and skill_scorecard.py doing read-time aggregation, not a merge-time hook. This false premise misdirects the insertion point and could lead the executor to reuse strategy.derive() (id/steps only) instead of building the token/usd/time/fix-round computation that strategy.observations() actually does, which the acceptance criterion needs.

The 'active' transition happens inside skills_registry.transition() (out of scope), called from two independent cli.py sites: 'skills promote' (line 377) and the generic 'skills transition <id> <state>' (line 414). If tagging source records with skill:<skill_id> is wired only into the promote branch, promoting the same skill via the generic transition command silently skips tagging, producing an inconsistent, hard-to-test gap depending on which equivalent CLI command was used.

memory_store.Record has no role field, but skills_registry.candidates() hard-filters on `role not in record.get('roles', [])`. candidates_from_memory groups gotcha/decision records that carry no role, so unless the spec defines how roles gets populated, propose() will emit skills with an empty roles list that can be promoted to active and pass all listed acceptance tests, yet are never selectable by any role at runtime — a dead skill a human reviewer would reject.

'tags task_class:<x>, band:<b>, strategy:<name>, outcome first_pass|fix_rounds:<n>' is ambiguous: Record already has a dedicated top-level outcome field, but the sentence structure reads as if outcome were a fourth tag. Divergent implementations (outcome as Record.outcome vs. outcome as a literal tag string) would both satisfy a loosely-written acceptance test while producing incompatible record shapes for `orchestrator memory strategies` to aggregate.

suggested_spec_changes: State explicitly that merge-time strategy derivation is new code to add inside daemon.py's merge_reviewed/_merge_reviewed_one (after the existing stamp(t['id'], 'merged_at') guard and only on result.get('status')=='merged'), reusing the per-task computation from strategy.observations() rather than implying it already exists.

Name the exact call site(s) where skill:<skill_id> tagging must be wired — either both cli.py promotion paths (line 377 and 414), or require skill_learning.py to expose a single tag_sources(skill_id, root) function that both paths call — so promotion-to-active is tagged consistently regardless of which CLI command performed it.

Specify how candidates_from_memory should populate the learned skill's `roles` and `task_classes` fields given that memory_store.Record has no role attribute, so the resulting proposal is actually selectable by skill_router/skills_registry.candidates() once promoted.
Clarify that the strategy record's `outcome` is the existing top-level Record.outcome field set to 'first_pass' or 'fix_rounds:<n>', separate from the three task_class/band/strategy tags.
